venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, Doha
venues.note: The group's quiet precision, dropped into the restored heart of the old city.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 5-Star (2025, sixth consecutive year)

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Doha
venues.note: The surest hands in the city, service you never have to think about, on its own beach.

venues.name: Raffles Doha
venues.note: Qatar's first all-suite house, inside the crossed-sabre towers, theatre with Raffles butlers.

venues.name: Rosewood Doha
venues.note: A soaring twin-tower newcomer that took a Forbes Five-Star in its first year.

venues.name: Sharq Village & Spa, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
venues.note: A low-slung Qatari 'village' by the sea, the calm, traditional counterpoint to the towers.

venues.name: Four Seasons Resort and Residences at The Pearl-Qatar
venues.note: A marina-side resort address on the man-made island, with Four Seasons ease throughout.

venues.name: The Chedi Katara Hotel & Resort, Doha
venues.note: GHM's understated design ideal beside the cultural village and its private beach.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Doha
venues.note: A grand marina resort with its own beach and yacht berths, classic Ritz-Carlton scale.

venues.name: The St. Regis Doha
venues.note: A palatial Gulf-front retreat with the signature St. Regis butler on every floor.

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Doha Lusail
venues.note: New-city grandeur on the Lusail waterfront, polished, spacious, of the moment.

venues.name: The Ned Doha
venues.note: A landmark government building reborn as a members'-club-and-hotel with real buzz.

venues.name: Mondrian Doha
venues.note: Maximalist, design-forward drama for the member who wants the volume turned up.

venues.name: W Doha
venues.note: A high-energy design house in the business district, for celebrations, not quiet nights.

venues.name: Banyan Tree Doha
venues.note: A spa-led vertical retreat with a sky-high pool over the downtown skyline.

venues.name: Marsa Malaz Kempinski, The Pearl-Doha
venues.note: A palace-scaled island house at the gateway to The Pearl, unabashedly grand.

venues.name: Fairmont Doha
venues.note: The second of the crossed-sabre towers, gold-leaf glamour on a grand scale.

venues.name: Banana Island Resort Doha by Anantara
venues.note: A ferry-only island escape with over-water villas, the closest thing to a beach holiday off Doha.

venues.name: The Plaza Doha, LXR Hotels & Resorts
venues.note: A jewel-box LXR house in the walkable downtown quarter, all quiet polish.

venues.name: InterContinental Doha Beach & Spa
venues.note: A long-established beach resort with the city's largest private stretch of sand.

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay
venues.note: A polished business-district tower with Waldorf Astoria service at a gentler price.

venues.name: IDAM by Alain Ducasse
venues.note: Ducasse's French-Mediterranean, on the museum's top floor, with Doha Bay filling the glass.
credentials: MENA's 50 Best #44 (2026, Best Restaurant in Qatar)

venues.name: Alba
venues.note: Piedmontese cooking of real refinement inside the crossed-sabre towers, Doha's newest star.

venues.name: Jamavar
venues.note: The Leela's grand pan-Indian house, the first Indian restaurant to win a Doha star.

venues.name: Hoppers
venues.note: Sri Lankan and South Indian home cooking, hoppers, kari and roti done with real soul.

venues.name: Isaan
venues.note: Northeastern Thai cooking with genuine fire and fragrance, a Bib-listed favourite.

venues.name: Jiwan
venues.note: Modern Qatari cooking under the museum's desert-rose roof, heritage, elevated.

venues.name: Argan
venues.note: Generous, aromatic Moroccan cooking, tagines and pastilla with a proper hand.

venues.name: Mila
venues.note: Bright Mediterranean and Levantine sharing plates in the Rosewood's newest room.

venues.name: Baron
venues.note: Characterful, generous Mediterranean cooking, a Beirut name that earned its Bib in Doha.

venues.name: Fenyal
venues.note: Vibrant, pocket-friendly Khaleeji cooking, falafel, lamb kofta and proper Arabic coffee.

venues.name: Nobu Doha
venues.area: Four Seasons Hotel Doha, West Bay
venues.note: The largest Nobu in the world, floating over the Gulf, the black cod that conquered the planet.

venues.name: Zuma Doha
venues.note: The izakaya benchmark that never empties, precise, buzzy, endlessly reliable.

venues.name: Hakkasan Doha
venues.note: The Cantonese standard-bearer, dim sum and lacquered duck in a low-lit lattice room.

venues.name: Morimoto Doha
venues.note: Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's Japanese, staged with Mondrian theatre.

venues.name: COYA Doha
venues.note: Peruvian colour and pisco energy, ceviche, anticuchos and a room that never quiets.

venues.name: La Mar Doha by Gastón Acurio
venues.area: InterContinental Doha Beach & Spa, West Bay
venues.note: Gastón Acurio's seaside Peruvian, bright cebiches and a long beachfront terrace.

venues.name: La Petite Maison (LPM) Doha
venues.note: Riviera cooking and a room that has never gone out of fashion, the Niçoise classic.

venues.name: Carbone Doha
venues.note: The New York Italian-American theatre, tableside Caesar, veal parm and red sauce, done grandly.

venues.name: Gymkhana Doha
venues.note: The Sethi family's colonial-club Indian, smoke, spice and swagger, carried from Mayfair.

venues.name: Masala Library Doha
venues.note: Jiggs Kalra's progressive Indian, familiar flavours, reimagined with a light modern hand.

venues.name: Dalchini
venues.note: Indian-Chinese and pan-Asian comfort cooking with a devoted local following.

venues.name: Em Sherif Doha
venues.note: Beirut's grand Lebanese table, an endless, generous procession of mezze.

venues.name: Curiosa by Jean-Georges
venues.note: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's playful, produce-led cooking in a jewel-box island room.

venues.name: Shanghai Me Doha
venues.note: 1930s-Shanghai glamour and pan-Asian cooking with real intent.

venues.name: Dar Yema
venues.note: Qatari home cooking preserved and served with pride, a rare taste of the real thing.

venues.name: Museum of Islamic Art
venues.note: I.M. Pei's last great commission, rising from its own island, the finest museum of Islamic art anywhere, and the building that told the world Doha was serious.
credentials: Designed by I.M. Pei, his final museum commission

venues.name: National Museum of Qatar
venues.note: Jean Nouvel's interlocking 'desert rose' discs, wrapped around the royal palace, the nation's story told inside one of the most photographed buildings on earth.

venues.name: Souq Waqif
venues.note: The old trading heart of Doha, faithfully restored to its mud-rendered walls and lantern-lit lanes, where the city still comes to eat, haggle and sit past midnight.

venues.name: Katara Cultural Village
venues.note: Qatar's largest cultural quarter, galleries, an opera house and a 5,000-seat marble amphitheatre by the sea, all in one walkable seafront village.

venues.name: Msheireb Museums
venues.note: Four restored heritage houses at the centre of the rebuilt old town, including Bin Jelmood House, one of the few museums anywhere to confront the Indian Ocean slave trade.

venues.name: The Pearl
venues.note: A four-square-kilometre island of marinas and Riviera arcades, the first ground in Qatar a foreigner could ever own, and the city's most European evening stroll.

venues.name: Doha Corniche
venues.note: The seven-kilometre crescent promenade that frames the whole city, walk it at dusk, dhows on one side and the West Bay skyline on the other.

venues.name: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
venues.note: The world's deepest collection of modern and contemporary Arab art, nine thousand works, and the first museum of its kind in the region.
credentials: World's largest collection of modern and contemporary Arab art

venues.name: 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum
venues.note: The Middle East's first sports museum and one of the largest Olympic collections on earth, every Games torch since 1936, beside Khalifa Stadium.

venues.name: Khor Al Adaid (the Inland Sea)
venues.note: One of the few places on the planet where the sea runs straight into the dunes, a protected inland sea reached only by 4x4 across the sand. A day trip your advisor arranges end to end.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, Khor Al-Adaid Natural Reserve

venues.name: Lusail Boulevard & Marina
venues.note: Qatar's built-from-nothing future city, a mile-long illuminated boulevard, the crossed-sabre Katara Towers and a waterfront that only switches on after dark.

venues.name: Jiwan & the MIA Park
venues.note: The parkland strung between the two great museums, sculpture by the water (Serra's '7'), the MIA café, and the city's best skyline picnic at sunset.

venues.name: Nobu Doha rooftop lounge
venues.note: The bar level of the largest Nobu in the world, a three-storey pavilion over the Gulf, cocktails and tapas with the West Bay skyline in the glass.
credentials: Within Four Seasons Hotel Doha (Forbes 5-Star, MICHELIN One Key)

venues.name: Ambar, Mandarin Oriental
venues.note: The quietly assured lounge in the group's Msheireb house, considered cocktails and artisanal bites, in the calmest, most central address in the city.
credentials: Within Mandarin Oriental, Doha (Forbes 5-Star, MICHELIN One Key)

venues.name: The rooftop bar at Raffles Doha
venues.note: Live soul and jazz and 360-degree views from inside the crossed-sabre towers, the highest, most theatrical drink in the new city.
credentials: Within Raffles Doha (Forbes 5-Star, MICHELIN Two Keys)

venues.name: The lounge bar at Rosewood Doha
venues.note: A polished sky-lounge in the twin-tower newcomer that took a Forbes Five-Star in its first year, a smart, contemporary place to begin the evening.
credentials: Within Rosewood Doha (Forbes 5-Star, MICHELIN One Key)
